questions.question: Which is the largest area of UK public spending by function?

options.B: Social protection, such as pensions and benefits
options.D: Public order and safety

questions.why: HM Treasury's PESA functional breakdown consistently shows social protection as the largest spending function.

questions.question: After social protection, which function usually takes the next biggest share of UK public spending?

options.D: Environment protection

questions.why: In PESA, health is consistently the second-largest spending function after social protection.

questions.question: In recent decades, total UK public spending has usually been roughly what share of national income (GDP)?

options.D: About 70 to 80%

questions.why: OBR and ONS figures put total managed expenditure at around 35 to 45% of GDP outside exceptional years such as 2020-21.

questions.question: Spending on a service rose in cash terms over twenty years. What else must you know to say it grew in real terms?

options.B: Whether it rose faster than inflation
options.D: Nothing; cash growth is real growth

questions.why: Real-terms growth means growth after adjusting for rising prices, so cash increases can hide a real fall.

questions.question: Which single tax raises the most money for the UK government?

options.D: Fuel duty

questions.why: HMRC and OBR receipts data show income tax is the largest single source of tax revenue.

questions.question: Which three taxes together raise more than half of UK government receipts?

options.A: Income tax, National Insurance and VAT
options.B: Council tax, stamp duty and fuel duty
options.C: Corporation tax, tobacco duty and alcohol duty
options.D: Inheritance tax, capital gains tax and air passenger duty

questions.why: OBR figures show income tax, NICs and VAT together make up well over half of total receipts.

questions.question: When UK public spending is higher than receipts in a year, how is the gap mainly covered?

options.C: A special one-off tax every year
options.D: Selling public land

questions.why: The gap is public sector net borrowing, financed mainly by issuing government debt such as gilts, which is not a tax.

questions.question: Which of these is a government receipt that is NOT a tax?

options.D: Interest and dividends the government receives

questions.why: ONS and OBR count interest and dividends as non-tax receipts, separate from taxes like VAT or corporation tax.

questions.question: In ONS household statistics, which income fifth pays the most tax in pounds per household?

options.D: All fifths pay about the same

questions.why: ONS Effects of Taxes and Benefits shows the richest fifth pays by far the most tax in cash terms per household.

questions.question: As a share of their disposable income, which households lose the most to indirect taxes like VAT and duties?

options.D: It is the same for every fifth

questions.why: ONS consistently finds indirect taxes take a larger share of disposable income for the poorest fifth because they spend more of their income.

questions.question: HMRC figures show the top 1% of income taxpayers pay roughly what share of all income tax?

options.D: More than three quarters

questions.why: HMRC income tax liabilities statistics have shown the top 1% paying roughly 25 to 30% of income tax for over a decade.

questions.question: A chart shows the richest fifth's share of all tax paid. What does that share measure?

options.A: The percentage of their income they pay in tax
options.B: The portion of total tax revenue that comes from them
options.C: The income tax rate for top earners
options.D: The tax a typical person in that group pays

questions.why: A share of total revenue is a different measure from a household's tax as a percentage of income or a personal tax rate.

questions.question: Someone pays the 40% higher rate of income tax. Does 40% of their whole income go in income tax?

options.B: No, 40% applies only to income above the higher-rate threshold
options.D: No, it is 40% of their household's spending

questions.why: UK income tax is banded, so the higher rate applies only to the slice of income above the threshold and the average rate is lower.

questions.question: In ONS household tax statistics, which of these counts as an indirect tax?

options.D: VAT

questions.why: ONS classes VAT as indirect (paid through spending) and income tax, employee NICs and council tax as direct taxes.

questions.question: A page says 'a household earning £35,000 pays £X tax', calculated from tax rules. What is this?

options.A: An illustration worked out from the rules, not a measured average of real households
options.B: The official average tax for all UK households
options.C: A figure measured from HMRC records of that household
options.D: The tax paid by the median household in a survey

questions.why: A calculated example applies rules to an assumed household, whereas measured figures like ONS averages come from surveys and records of real households.

questions.question: Average pay rose 20% in cash terms while prices rose 25% over the same period. What happened to real pay?

options.D: It stayed exactly the same

questions.why: When prices rise faster than cash pay, pay after inflation falls.

questions.question: Employment rose in the years after a new policy began. What does a chart of employment alone show?

options.B: Employment changed, but not why it changed
options.D: Employment would have fallen without the policy

questions.why: A time series shows change over time; attributing it to a cause needs separate evidence that rules out other factors.

questions.question: Over recent decades, how has the share of UK jobs in manufacturing changed?

options.A: It has fallen while service jobs grew
options.D: It now makes up most jobs

questions.why: ONS workforce jobs data show manufacturing's share of jobs falling for decades as services expanded.

questions.question: In England, which is the most common housing tenure?

options.D: Living rent-free

questions.why: The English Housing Survey shows owner occupiers make up roughly two thirds of households.

questions.question: Since the early 2000s, what has happened to the share of English households renting privately?

options.D: It has fallen to almost zero

questions.why: The English Housing Survey shows private renting rising from about 10% of households around 2000 to around 19 to 20%.

questions.question: Which country is usually the most visited overseas destination for UK residents?

options.D: Italy

questions.why: ONS Travel trends consistently show Spain as the top destination for UK residents' visits abroad.

questions.question: Why might a series of UK residents' holidays abroad show a gap or break around 2020?

options.B: The pandemic disrupted travel and suspended survey data collection
options.C: The survey switched to counting only domestic trips
options.D: Figures for that year were deliberately deleted

questions.why: The International Passenger Survey was suspended in 2020 during COVID-19, so figures for that period are missing or not comparable.

questions.question: In England, infant classes (ages 5 to 7) with one school teacher are legally limited to how many pupils?
questions.why: The infant class size limit in England caps such classes at 30 pupils per school teacher, with limited exceptions.

questions.question: In England's state schools, which phase usually has the larger average class size?

options.D: Neither; classes are not measured

questions.why: DfE school census statistics show average primary class sizes (around 26 to 27) above secondary (around 22 to 23).
